title: 2007 HMMT February General Round 1 Problem 4
statement: Let \(a\) and \(b\) be integer solutions to \(17 a+6 b=13\). What is the smallest possible positive value for \(a-b\) ?

solutions.text: 17. First group as \(17(a-b)+23 b=13\). Taking this equation modulo 23, we get \(-6(a-b) \equiv\) \(-10(\bmod 23)\). Since -4 is an inverse of -6 modulo 23 , then we multiply to get \((a-b) \equiv 17(\bmod 23)\). Therefore, the smallest possible positive value for \((a-b)\) is 17 . This can be satisfied by \(a=5, b=-12\).
